title: Our climate models have a big, dangerous blind spot
abstract: Climate change itself is increasingly fueling climate change. Rising concentrations of greenhouse gases are driving up global temperatures, setting off dangerous feedback loops that we have not fully accounted for in our climate models—or our emissions-reduction goals. Scientists have long warned that warming would propel further warming in various ways, but a growing number of observations and studies are at last providing a sharper sense of just how powerful these cascading effects could be. And, by extension, they’re showing how much faster the planet may warm in this century. A study in Environmental Research Letters in September, synthesizing the results of previous papers, found that the additional carbon dioxide and methane released from thawing permafrost, intensifying wildfires, hotter lakes and reservoirs , and wetter, warmer wetlands alone could drive global average temperatures up 0.2 °C to 0.4 °C this century. That would come on top of the 2.6°C of warming above preindustrial levels that modelers are already expecting through 2100. The additional heat could subject many of the world’s cities to monthslong heat waves and expose hundreds of millions of people to flooding. None of the models that inform the major UN climate reports, which assess how much the planet will likely warm under various emissions scenarios, account for all these feedback effects. Many of them don’t incorporate any. That leaves a huge blind spot in our understanding of how much the world could actually warm in the coming decades—and how rapidly nations will need to slash emissions to stay within critical boundaries. A separate analysis published in One Earth in March , which examined what the feedback problem means for our international climate goals, concluded that the world may be much further off track than is widely believed. It found that just three regional sources of warming-driven emissions—thawing permafrost, increasing fires in boreal forests, and warming tropical wetlands—may shorten by as much as 25% the time before the planet consistently breaches the 1.5 °C and 2 °C warming thresholds. Our climate models and the UN’s reports clearly need to be updated to better represent these effects. Nations must also step up their efforts to reduce emissions to reflect this improving understanding of the dangers we face, says Sam Abernethy, the lead author of the paper and a climate scientist at Spark Climate Solutions, a San Francisco–based nonprofit research group. At least some of this is starting to happen. Spark kick-started an initiative, called the Warming-Induced Greenhouse Gas Emissions Model Intercomparison Project , through which more than 20 international teams are running the same set of analyses on different models to develop greater understanding of feedback effects’ potential power. Researchers involved hope that the UN will incorporate those results into its next major climate assessment, due out in 2029. That report will update estimates of the remaining emissions that can be released before the world crosses key temperature thresholds. But what is already clear is that the planet is rapidly warming and that nations haven’t done nearly enough to cut fossil-fuel pollution. And even if we did manage to halt it, warming-driven emissions could continue. So a number of the research groups involved in the recent studies have started to explore what nations could do to get feedback emissions under control. title: Creating AI value with enterprise context
abstract: Across a business, any number of AI platforms, systems, and tools may be at work simultaneously—for example, AI-powered customer platforms, conversational assistants, and workflow and process automation tools. Each one is sophisticated, advanced, and quick to respond. But, when set to work, the outcomes and actions that emerge may be wrong, confused, or lacking a proper understanding of the business. Many organizations find themselves in this situation—and it could be one of key reasons they struggle to extract returns on their AI investments. DOWNLOAD THE REPORT An MIT Technology Review Insights poll finds that while every organization surveyed is using AI today to some degree, fewer than one in five (16%) are extracting transformative value from their deployments. The largest percentage of respondents (40%) say they are seeing moderate gains in specific tasks or teams, while 21% report meaningful gains, leaving 23% that are seeing minimal returns or none at all. Companies are mostly still piloting AI use cases (according to 38% of respondents) or using it to assist employees’ work with tools like co-pilots or chat assistants (35%). Just 12% of enterprises have AI agents in production and 3% say they are using AI to do most of the work in key processes. “There’s a big gap between what the models are capable of and how the models are actually being useful inside organizations,” says Prukalpa Sankar, co-founder of Atlan. “For every real-life intent and purpose, artificial general intelligence is already here. It’s just not really useful in most companies today.” The missing layer, Sankar says, is context, or how well AI understands a business. A context layer is the architectural infrastructure that sits between an organization’s business systems (for example, systems of record and data, and its AI platforms). It translates enterprise intelligence into governed, machine-usable context for AI agents or models and helps knowledge compound. “Without a context layer for AI, it’s almost like you’re hiring the smartest intern in the world, blindfolding them, and throwing them into your organization,” Sankar says. title: Industrial Intelligence: The next growth opportunity for manufacturing
abstract: Every manufacturer has its own industrial intelligence. Some is documented, and some resides in the knowledge of experienced workers. Consider an experienced operator preparing to restart a line after a changeover. The machine settings matter, but so does knowing how a particular material behaves, what happened during the previous shift, and when an apparently minor variation deserves a closer look. A procedure can describe the sequence, but successful execution depends on the judgment that comes from experience and the organization’s accumulated know-how. That combination is industrial intelligence: a manufacturer’s accumulated know-how, operating practices, production data, and understanding of its own business. The opportunity now is to make more of that intelligence available wherever decisions are made, then connect it to the physical world of manufacturing. The strategic destination is not more agents, but rather to turn the existing business intelligence into an engine for profitable growth. Individual knowledge can be translated into organizational advantage Expertise has limited reach when it stays with one person, inside one system, or within one plant. Leaders now must determine how to extend that reach without stripping away the context that makes the knowledge useful. For example, an engineer evaluating a process change needs more than a production record. They need to understand the circumstances behind it: the equipment configuration, the quality requirements, and the trade-offs an operator made. Connecting those elements can help people apply experience beyond the place where it originated. When individual knowledge becomes widely accessible, innovation can spread to the maintenance workshop, the planning office, the engineering team, and the production floor. More people can contribute because more people can work with what the organization knows. But access to knowledge is only part of the opportunity. Manufacturing ultimately is physical, and it depends on materials, machines, and products. When intelligence participates in action Physical AI describes systems that can perceive conditions, reason about them, and take action within the physical world. By connecting machines and processes, manufacturers get a clearer view of what is happening on the factory floor. Agents can then reason on top of that information to identify patterns, predict problems, and determine the best course of action. Physical AI brings business intelligence into the physical process, allowing machines and systems to respond to changing conditions. Consider a robotic-handling operation encountering variation in the parts arriving at its station. Vision can help the system assess a part’s position. A model informed by the material and task can help determine an appropriate movement. Connected controls can then execute an adjustment within validated limits. The value is not merely seeing the variation; it is responding appropriately. The same principle applies to quality operations. When Toyota Industries connected previously fragmented paint shop data, engineering and operations teams were given the context needed to understand defect drivers. The company reports that analysis cycles fell from five days to under four hours, while its pilot reduced relevant paint defects by about 25%. The breakthrough was not simply identifying another signal; it was helping people understand why defects were occurring and respond before the outcome was locked in. This is the type of situation where industrial intelligence has become essential. Data may reveal what is happening, but industrial intelligence provides the context for what should happen, which constraints cannot be breached, and when uncertainty requires human judgment. title: How solid-state transformers could help power the AI boom
abstract: Transformers are a crucial but nearly invisible part of our grid. The devices help efficiently move power across long distances, but they’re complicated and in short supply. And given that their basic design hasn’t changed much for about a century, they could use an upgrade. As the world races to meet rising electricity demand from EVs, data centers, and more, researchers and companies are looking to modernize transformers. New, solid-state versions could help relieve some of the supply concerns and make sure the grid can handle the growing pressure. Conventional transformers generally rely on huge amounts of specialized steel alloys and miles of copper wire to do their work of transferring electricity between circuits. Solid-state models, in comparison, combine magnetic components with high-power semiconductors, making them more compact and allowing for more control over the flow of electricity. These devices are still in development, and can’t replace all traditional transformers today, especially the largest ones that work at the high voltages necessary for long-distance transmission. But a new generation of transformer technology could be a crucial part of our future grid. The grid’s backbone Moving electricity through the grid isn’t perfectly efficient: As electricity flows through power lines, some gets lost as heat. How much varies—the higher the voltage, the lower the current, and the less electricity gets lost. So a key function for the grid is stepping voltage up and down. Consider, for example, your local solar plant. For that electricity to efficiently travel to your home hundreds of miles away, it needs to reach a higher voltage than what’s generated by the solar plant. Enter transformers. In its path from the power plant to your outlets, electricity might go through one transformer at the solar farm and another at a substation nearby, stepping up the voltage twice to reach a high enough level to travel on high-voltage transmission lines. Solar panels also produce direct current (DC) electricity, which needs to be converted to alternating current (AC) via an inverter before it flows into a transformer. Closer to its destination, the voltage will be stepped down again, probably at least twice: once at another substation and again at a smaller transformer in your neighborhood. If you’re in the US, electricity from a solar plant might be converted to AC by an inverter at around 480 volts, get stepped up to 115,000 volts for the transmission lines, and finally get stepped back down to 120 volts and 240 volts for your home. Conventional transformers do this work using what essentially amount to loops of wire. The core of a transformer is typically made of a special type of steel called grain-oriented electrical steel. Coils of copper wire sit on either end of that core. The number of loops in each coil determines the voltage on either end of the transformer: If there are more loops on the secondary coil than the primary, the voltage steps up, and if there are fewer, it steps down. When incoming electricity passes through loops on the upstream end of the transformer, that forms a magnetic field in the core. That field induces a voltage in the loops on the other side of the device, which is what allows the energy to continue flowing at a new voltage. This process is called magnetic induction. Transformers form the backbone of electricity transmission and distribution, says Srdjan Lukic, a professor of electrical and computer engineering at North Carolina State University. In addition to doing the job of stepping up and down voltage, transformers also often provide what’s called galvanic isolation, meaning there’s no direct electrical path flowing through them. That can help limit disturbances from moving through the grid, improving safety. title: Systems Thinking Is Vital in the Age of AI
abstract: Modern engineering projects increasingly combine human judgment with machine capability. An engineer can define a problem, then ask an artificial intelligence tool to search relevant research and technical standards, generate design options, test them in simulation, and compare the results. The engineer can then bring the results to specialists who understand the parts AI cannot judge on its own, such as whether a design can be built safely, whether it makes sense in a particular setting, or how it might affect its users. The final decision about whether and how to move forward remains a human responsibility. AI can help engineers do early project steps that once required several people with different technical skills. The engineer’s role is therefore expanding from performing each technical step to deciding how people, machines, and specialists’ knowledge should work together on the project. The problem, not the title Engineering has always been divided into disciplines, and for good reasons. Electrical, mechanical, civil, software, and other engineering fields require deep knowledge that takes years to develop. AI does not replace that need. It simply changes how easily engineers can explore the parts of a problem that sit outside their own specialty. Consider a software engineer working on a medical device . AI can help the engineer review relevant biomedical research, understand unfamiliar terms, analyze data, and build an early model. That does not make the engineer a physician or biomedical expert. It allows the engineer to ask better questions before working with the experts. The same is true in energy , transportation, manufacturing, and many other fields. A problem might begin as a software issue and then quickly involve hardware, safety measures, economics, human behavior, and regulations. Engineers do not need to master every field; they need to recognize which expertise the problem requires and bring the right people and tools together. The importance of systems thinking Systems thinking thus becomes especially important. It requires looking at the whole problem: understanding how its parts affect one another, identifying constraints and failure points, and making trade-offs. AI adds a new element to the process. Engineers must decide not only how the technical parts fit together but also what work to give to AI, what a person must check, when a specialist should make a decision, and when the problem needs to be redefined. An engineer’s value is not in knowing everything. It is in knowing how to frame the problem, how to ask the right questions, how to test the answers, and when another expert must lead the project. This aspect is crucial because technical challenges in engineering are seldom static. As new insights emerge, objectives might shift, unseen limitations can surface, and the initial premise might prove flawed. Rather than rigidly following the starting specifications, an effective engineer adapts and refines the scope as a deeper understanding of the system develops. Thus, engineering extends beyond mastering technical concepts; it is an adaptable, structured approach to navigating evolving challenges. New evidence can change the goal, reveal a hidden constraint, or show that the original hypothesis was wrong. Effective engineers go beyond merely acting on the initial problem statement. They update it as the system becomes better understood. In that sense, engineering is not only a body of technical knowledge, it is also a disciplined way of thinking about a project. It can summarize research without understanding which evidence is strongest, or optimize a design for the wrong goal. Such limits make human expertise more important, not less. abstract: This article is brought to you by VicOne . A mobile robot slows for someone in a hallway. A collaborative arm eases its movement as a worker approaches. A humanoid pauses to let a person pass. Each response depends on information about the robot or its surroundings: a distance reading, a position estimate, or a stop signal. But what happens when one of those inputs is wrong, and the robot still responds exactly as designed? The mobile robot reads the hallway as clear while someone is still there. The arm estimates that the worker is farther away. The humanoid does not receive a stop signal as a person crosses its path. In each case, a fault could cause that mismatch. So could deliberate manipulation . At VicOne LAB R7 , we examine how manipulated inputs can change robot behavior — and what that means for the systems meant to keep people safe. How an untrusted input can change a robot’s behavior A robot does more than measure its surroundings. It may interpret what it sees and hears to decide what to do next. Information placed in its environment can therefore influence its actions. Published research shows how this can happen. In a study of vision-language-action (VLA) models , a patch in a camera’s view reduced task success in simulated robot tests. FreezeVLA found that an adversarial image could cause tested models to ignore later instructions. Although the studies used different methods, both demonstrate how visual input can interfere with a robot’s intended task. title: I Used AI to Fake a Scientific Paper. Here’s What Happened
abstract: Science has a spam problem. And the spam filter is getting clogged up. According to all reports, academic publishing is drowning in what has come to be called AI slop: low-quality, mass-produced content generated with AI. By 2025, an estimated 57 percent of all published academic articles exhibited detectable evidence of large language model (LLM) influence, a massive jump from 12 percent in 2023. What’s more, over 12 percent of Nature Communications reviews were found to be completely AI-generated in 2025. Given that for every 40 papers showing statistical evidence of AI usage in 2025, only one formally disclosed it , these figures likely grossly underestimate LLM involvement today. Of course, evidence of AI use doesn’t necessarily mean a paper is slop. But some estimates suggest that hundreds of thousands of fake, often AI-generated, publications are now produced annually. “It’s not just the [scientific] record under threat, it’s science as a whole,” warns Amanda Sulicz , IEEE’s research-integrity manager. “AI slop is completely eroding trust in science and every scientific process that we’ve worked for centuries to create.” Yet statistics and statements claiming that the problem is big—perhaps even existential for science—don’t really get the message across. Just how easy is it to use AI to create a convincing but completely fake paper? And without adding even more to the burden on stretched peer reviewers, who do this work on a volunteer basis, do publishers have the tools to keep AI slop out of the scientific record? Borrowing from the idea of “vibe coding,” in which programmers use natural-language prompts to generate code, I decided to “vibe-research” a made-up paper by prompting LLMs to generate hypotheses, code, and text with minimal human input. Then I asked Jenny Mahoney , managing editor of the multidisciplinary and open-access journal IEEE Access , if we could war-game an attempt to sneak my AI-generated monstrosity past her journal’s defenses. She and IEEE kindly agreed. The experiment would become a two-part test. First, whether someone with no special AI expertise could use off-the-shelf AI tools to generate a convincing paper describing research that had never been performed, and do it well enough to fool a publisher’s defenses. Then I would raise the stakes: What happens when more advanced AI systems don’t just write the paper but conduct underlying research? Along the way, the experiment became a window into how AI automation is transforming scientific discovery and forcing stakeholders to rethink the entire academic publishing system. Round 1: Creating the Forgery To give me a chance at creating a convincing fake, I gave myself permission to prompt multiple times (within reason). But to make the fight fair, I couldn’t access the most advanced paid versions of LLMs—only free ChatGPT (at the time, GPT-5.3/5.2 Mini) and Gemini (3 Flash). Moreover, I could not directly edit any output, nor ask for outside help from expert AI-prompt engineers. This needed to be an amateur effort, with the paper generated as much as possible by the LLMs alone. I assumed that using fake author names and affiliations would immediately raise a red flag, and I didn’t want to drag the names of established academics into the experiment, so the best bet was to name myself as the sole author. That choice limited me to subjects in which I had some academic experience. So I chose my Ph.D. topic from nearly two decades ago: optical solitons, which are individual light pulses that propagate without any change to their shape. title: Reddit is moving to “a logged-in-only experience,” CEO says
abstract: In the future, you won’t be able to use Reddit without logging in. Reddit CEO Steve Huffman confirmed the impending change in a letter (PDF) to shareholders today about Q3 performance. He said that Reddit is shifting “to a logged-in-only experience," adding: Moving to primarily logged-in will ensure our users have the best Reddit experience possible, and can find the content and communities most relevant to them. It is better for our business because we will have more signals for ads targeting, and being logged-in leads to higher engagement generally. It also allows us to protect access to Reddit’s extremely valuable corpus of data, and helps us better adapt to emerging regulations around the world. Huffman also said that the login requirement will help Reddit better retain new users. Read full article Comments

title: Microsoft fixes a Windows 11 annoyance as PC revenue declines
abstract: Microsoft is beginning the rollout of a Windows 11 preview update that finally addresses a persistent power user complaint with the operating system: the right-click menu that obliterated years of muscle memory on command locations and hid others behind an additional click. The timing is notable, as the announcement comes alongside Microsoft's quarterly financial report, which showed a continued decline in the business of selling Windows licenses for new PCs. The preview update, KB5127936 , is cumulative for Windows 11 versions 26H2 and 25H2. The update will be a gradual rollout before eventually moving on to a normal rollout for all Windows 11 devices once it reaches general availability. The highlight of the new update should calm annoyed users who have spent years with custom scripts and services in an attempt to shape Windows the way they would prefer it. Users will get a "customize menu" button that controls what commands appear when they right-click their mouse. Users can toggle built-in commands such as Send To or Create Shortcut on or off, rearrange what appears on the main menu, and control which third-party extensions show up in either the main or submenus. The gripe with the right-click menu had been that Microsoft hid familiar command locations behind a top row of icons while moving other familiar commands under the "Show more options" submenu. Now, Windows users can customize the whole thing around their habits. The original Windows 11 right-click menu is a mess. Credit: Microsoft The new preview also highlights a new Windows feature called Cloud Rebuild, a recovery option that can reinstall Windows 11 directly from the cloud, even when an existing Windows 11 fails to boot. Cloud Rebuild will pull the Windows 11 image and needed system drivers directly from Windows Update. Users will not need a custom recovery image or external media to reinstall Windows. There is an important distinction to note, however. Microsoft classifies Cloud Rebuild as a recovery option, but it behaves more like a fresh Windows install than a repair, as existing applications and files will not be included. Those worried about data security can sanitize entire system drives prior to reinstalling. For a full list of improvements coming to Windows 11, including changes to Xbox mode and settings, you can view the official Microsoft release announcement . Read full article Comments

title: Pentagon IG refuses to investigate Starlink/Starshield slowdown in Ukraine
abstract: The Pentagon inspector general's office declined a request from US senators to investigate restrictions recently imposed on the Ukraine military's use of SpaceX's satellite network. Ukraine, which uses SpaceX's Starlink service and the military version known as Starshield, said earlier this month that military drones lost satellite connectivity when traveling above 161 kilometers per hour (100 miles per hour). The limit was removed after about 10 days. Five Democratic and four Republican senators sent an October 15 letter to Department of Defense Inspector General Platte Moring, asking for a probe into the reported disruptions of Starlink and Starshield. The letter asked, among other things, "whether any restrictions on Starlink or Starshield services were directed, authorized, or implemented by SpaceX, the Department of Defense, or other US government entities; whether such restrictions were consistent with applicable US government contracts, and what actions, if any, the Department of Defense took in response." Read full article Comments

title: Trump declares robot imports a national security threat
abstract: President Donald Trump has declared the imports of foreign-made factory robots to be a national security threat—ordering new US negotiations with trading partners while holding out the possibility of imposing new tariffs on such robot imports in the future. Issued on October 28, Trump’s presidential proclamation represents heightened government scrutiny of foreign-made industrial robots that could complicate the manufacturing operations of major US corporations that rely on such robots. Those companies include Detroit automakers General Motors and Ford, electric vehicle manufacturer Tesla , and aerospace and defense giants like Boeing and Lockheed Martin. Trump’s proclamation describes industrial robots and machinery as being crucial for producing US military weapon systems along with representing a “driving force” behind all critical infrastructure sectors within the US economy. The proclamation cites an investigation under US Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick as having found that US imports of such robots “pose[] risks to the United States industrial base and threatens the long-term competitiveness of the United States in a sector that is increasingly vital to national security.” Read full article Comments

title: Trump ignored intel on China’s Nvidia spy to protect company’s stock, report says
abstract: Donald Trump apparently is so aligned with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang—who has become the president’s key advisor on AI —that he ignored intelligence indicating that Huang was the target of a “Chinese spy plot,” and did so partly to protect Nvidia’s stock. The New York Times spoke with people briefed on US intelligence agencies’ surveillance and granted them anonymity to discuss findings drawn from “classified intelligence.” According to sources, about a year ago, Trump was briefed that “Beijing was getting reports from someone with direct access” to Huang. That “someone” was Alice Huang, or Huang Le, a Chinese citizen and former top executive at a Singapore cloud company called Megaspeed. According to sources, the US had already suspected that Alice Huang—who is not related to Jensen Huang—was helping China evade export controls to gain access to high-end Nvidia chips through Megaspeed. But it alarmed investigators to discover that she may have used her role at Megaspeed to gain direct access to Jensen Huang. It’s now believed she may have leveraged that closeness to feed China intel not only on one of America’s leading AI companies, but also to influence Trump’s thinking on AI. As Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent noted last month ahead of Trump’s AI talks with China President Xi Jinping, “the president is completely aligned with Jensen Huang, the CEO of Nvidia.” Read full article Comments

title: Turning a solar power system into its own backup
abstract: Rather than directly converting photons into electricity, concentrated solar energy uses mirrors to turn sunlight into heat, which can then be used to drive traditional generating turbines. Up to about a decade ago, there was a case to be made that concentrated solar energy had a bright future, as improvements in heat storage had turned it into a way to generate power around the clock. It wasn't to be. While concentrated solar costs fell enough to compete with nuclear power, the price of photovoltaics plunged, making solar panels the cheapest source of power in most locations. Currently, if you have a good site to generate solar power, then the economics of PV panels are hard to beat. That has left us needing to build a mixture of other facilities—typically batteries and natural gas facilities—to handle overnight needs or weather-driven shortfalls. But a small company is promising that it can help avoid the need to build a separate facility. Its version of concentrated solar is designed so that a fossil-fueled backup system shares most of the generating hardware with the solar side. Read full article Comments

title: Kalshi and its co-founders face felony charges for violating Utah gambling laws
abstract: The Trump administration is trying to stop Utah from enforcing its gambling ban against Kalshi, making Utah the 10th state sued by the US government agency that regulates prediction markets. Meanwhile, Utah Attorney General Derek Brown filed criminal charges in a state court against Kalshi and its founders on Wednesday. The attorney general's office provided us with court filings listing charges against KalshiEX, LLC , Kalshi co-founder and CEO Tarek Mansour , and Kalshi co-founder and COO Luana Lopes Lara . The company and two co-founders each face 13 felony charges and one misdemeanor for violating gambling laws. The charges are based on sports bets offered on Kalshi between September 13 and September 24. "The state did not issue arrest warrants for Monsour and Lopes Lara. Instead, they have been issued summons to respond to the charges in Third District Court in Salt Lake County," The Salt Lake Tribune wrote . Read full article Comments

title: Google admits AI search makes less money, but it's fixing that with more ads
abstract: Google parent Alphabet reported its Q3 financial results on Wednesday afternoon, showing a healthy rise in revenue for the months of July to September. But the company's stock price has taken a beating, marking one of the largest post-earnings drops in its history. It comes down to several troubling aspects of the new report, including an admission by the company that AI search isn't earning as much as organic search, and despite that, Google expects to spend even more on AI next year. The company took in almost $128 billion in Q3 2026, earning more than $26 billion in net income. These may sound like good numbers, but financial markets are not impressed. While revenue is up 25 percent versus last year, net income is almost $9 billion lower. As of this story's publication, the stock price is down almost 12 percent, and it was down about 13 percent earlier in the day. While revenue was up 25 percent year over year, analysts expected more. Google reported earnings per share of $2.12, but the consensus projection ahead of Wednesday was $3.02. Google's Cloud products actually beat expectations, crossing $30 billion in revenue. That's about a billion more than analyst guesses. Read full article Comments

title: Massive leak exposes 41,000 DHS workers and undercover ICE agents
abstract: An unprecedented leak of Department of Homeland Security records has exposed details of more than 41,000 employees or contractors who work for the department and its constituent agencies. The records include email addresses, phone numbers, and office addresses, but also references to internal systems and sensitive information on undercover and surveillance programs. In all, the leak provides a map of how DHS is organized and how it operates. The records, which span DHS itself as well as seven component agencies, including Immigration and Customs Enforcement and US Customs and Border Protection, were last updated on August 19, 2026. The transparency nonprofit Distributed Denial of Secrets and cybersecurity researcher and journalist maia arson crimew previewed the data for WIRED, which they say they obtained from a group calling itself the Department of Peace. DDoSecrets published the archive, which it calls “Icepick,” on Wednesday. In a press release, DDoSecrets says the data is from DHS's Okta login system. In a note with the files, the hackers wrote, “They have our information, so it’s only fair that we have theirs.” Read full article Comments

title: SpaceX no longer needs NASA, and that's a problem for America's space agency
abstract: For nearly a quarter of a century, Elon Musk and his essential partner at SpaceX, Gwynne Shotwell, viewed the United States government as El Dorado, the mythical city of gold. Like machete-wielding treasure hunters, Musk and Shotwell hacked through a tangled jungle filled with lurking carnivores such as Boeing and Lockheed Martin, as well as bean counters and regulators. Over time, against long odds, the pair cleared a path for SpaceX to contracts at NASA and the US military. They sued when things did not go their way. They hollered about unfair playing fields. Most importantly, they delivered quality space products to the US government for less. And so, after a while, SpaceX found El Dorado and a city of contracts. Read full article Comments

title: ULA's Vulcan rocket is set to return to flight on Friday the 13th
abstract: United Launch Alliance announced Wednesday it plans to return its Vulcan rocket to service on November 13, nine months after a solid rocket booster anomaly threw the company's 2026 launch schedule into oblivion. The return-to-flight mission will launch 40 satellites for the Amazon Leo broadband constellation, the first of 38 Vulcan flights Amazon has booked to deploy the bulk of its network. The mission will lift off from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, Florida, and ULA said the launch date is pending range approval. The launch is critical for ULA after its new flagship rocket suffered nozzle failures on its solid rocket boosters on two of its first four missions, most recently during a flight in February. In both cases, the rocket overcame the nozzle failure and completed its mission, but officials at the US Space Force, ULA's primary customer, lost confidence in Vulcan. Read full article Comments

title: As US ties fray, Europe plans first undersea cable link to Greenland
abstract: The European Union plans to create the first subsea Internet cable directly connecting Europe to Greenland. The Pan-Arctic Cable project could also extend to Canada and eventually link with Japan and South Korea, notably bypassing the United States. The Pan-Arctic Cable is described as a European Union flagship project in a European Commission joint communication published on October 20, 2026. The policy document describes a new European strategy for the Arctic that supports “a sovereign, secure and resilient submarine cable connection linking Greenland directly to the EU,” while also suggesting that “like-minded partners like Canada” could provide a stepping stone for future cable expansion toward Asia. “It is interesting that this project is even being considered, because five years ago it would have seemed like not a particularly commercially attractive proposition,” Elisabeth Braw , a senior fellow at the Atlantic Council who leads the Threats to the Global Maritime Order Initiative, told Ars. “But the fact that it's being considered is very much on trend and a sign of our times.” Read full article Comments

title: Peptide peddlers cheer as RFK Jr. unilaterally grants access, overruling FDA
abstract: Anti-vaccine Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy has unilaterally passed a rule that will allow specialty pharmacies to sell six specific peptide drugs, overruling scientists at the Food and Drug Administration. The peptides are popular among members of Kennedy's Make America Health Again movement, and many prominent MAHA figures and Kennedy allies sell them. Kennedy said he uses some of the peptides and called himself a "big fan." But FDA scientists continue to say there is insufficient evidence to show if they're effective, and they are potentially dangerous. In 2023, the safety concerns led the FDA to remove the six peptides from a list of drugs that can be made by specialty pharmacies called compounding pharmacies—which make customized formulations of drugs for patients, or, in cases such as this, specialty drugs in bulk. Kennedy's new rule sidesteps the need to formally undo that FDA action. The rule is titled "Enforcement Discretion Policy Regarding 503A Compounding Using Certain Peptide Bulk Drug Substances" and was made available Wednesday on the Federal Register , with the final publication date set for October 30. The rule does not change the regulatory status of the peptide; instead, it states the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) will no longer take enforcement action against compounding pharmacies for making the peptides, essentially giving them a green light to freely produce and sell them. Kennedy had quietly proposed this rule earlier this month. Read full article Comments

title: The last, best hope for space tourism just rolled onto a runway in Arizona
abstract: The private space tourism era looked so very promising five years ago. Blue Origin and Virgin Galactic had begun flying customers—real people with zero space experience—on suborbital missions. And at about the same time, private citizens were going to orbit for days at a time aboard SpaceX's Crew Dragon. But that was then. Consider the state of play today: It has been 10 months since Blue Origin's New Shepard spacecraft flew its last mission in January. The program was subsequently "paused," but let's be real. Blue Origin has moved on. New Shepard's engineering teams are now supporting the New Glenn rocket and Blue Moon lander programs. SpaceX flew its final free-flyer mission on Dragon, Fram2, in April 2025. A handful of non-NASA missions bound for space stations remain on the spacecraft's manifest, but all are likely to carry at least one government astronaut. Then Dragon will be retired. There is no credible timeline for SpaceX's Starship to fly humans into space from Earth. As for Virgin Galactic, the company flew its final suborbital mission on the VSS Unity spacecraft more than two years ago, in June 2024. So we are now 10 months, and counting, without a space tourism mission in the United States. Read full article Comments

title: Touchscreen MacBook Pro hands-on: OLED looks great on a Mac
abstract: LOS ANGELES—For about five minutes on an extremely crowded showroom floor, I got to take pictures of the new MacBook Pro and test out some of its new features. First impressions: It's not as much of a departure from the previous design as I expected, but the outstanding OLED display steals the show regardless. The first thing I noticed was that it's lighter. My daily driver is a 14-inch MacBook Pro (M1 Max), and it's a bit weighty for a 14-incher. Picking up the new model, I could immediately tell it was lighter. It's not like it's in a different general weight class, but it's a noticeable difference. Read full article Comments

title: Google announces Gemini 4 Carbon, its latest frontier AI model that you can't use
abstract: It's almost like Google's got something to prove after taking a break from releasing new frontier AI models earlier this year. Just two weeks after rolling out Gemini 4 Argon , Google has announced Gemini 4 Carbon . This isn't the Flash model equivalent we've been waiting for but, rather, is an improvement on Argon, and like that model, Google is working on a staged release that could take a while. Stop me if you've heard this one before: Google says its latest AI model reaches a new threshold in coding, agentic tasks, and scientific analysis. It's so capable, in fact, that Google can't let you use it just yet. Gemini 4 Carbon reportedly makes big gains in cybersecurity applications. Google says the model shows a "significant leap" in vulnerability detection, validation, and remediation. Carbon is also apparently twice as likely to generate code that is free of vulnerabilities versus Argon. Meanwhile, the Chrome team claims that Carbon is 10 times better at generating "high-quality" patches compared to non-Google models. Google also notes that Carbon has increased its score by 89 points on WebDev Arena , now ranking at number four on the leaderboard. Read full article Comments

title: Amazon turns its most capable smart speaker into a smart camera, too
abstract: Since debuting in 2019, Amazon's Echo Studio targeted users who wanted superior audio quality from their Alexa-based smart speaker. The latest Echo Studio adds another less-expected differentiator: an integrated camera. The Echo Studio with Home Camera, released alongside a pile of other Alexa devices today, doesn’t have many audio upgrades over the standard Echo Studio. Each speaker has one 3.75-inch high-excursion woofer and three full-range drivers. They both support Dolby Atmos and Amazon’s proprietary algorithm for adding a surround sound-like effect to stereo audio. Per the devices’ product pages, the speakers have lossless HD audio, Advanced Room Adaptation, and features for fighting noise distortion. Amazon announced the Advanced Room Adaptaion today, saying that the feature “continuously tunes the sound to your space, automatically adapting to the room's acoustics.” Both speakers have four-microphone arrays and the same AZ3 Pro processor that Amazon introduced a year ago . The processor has an AI accelerator for using Amazon's Alexa+ generative AI chatbot . Read full article Comments

title: Cadillac Escalade IQ review: Huge battery, huge range, huge SUV
abstract: “Please have at least 125 miles of range left when we pick it up.” That request from the people who look after the Cadillac press cars wasn’t going to be hard to honor. The electric Escalade IQ arrived with an indicated range of 440 miles (708 km), and with a full week of work to squeeze in, getting anywhere close to needing to recharge it seemed unlikely. With more than 200 kWh of lithium-ion battery between its axles, range is one thing the big electric Caddy needn’t worry about. Designed and debuted during a time of greater EV optimism, the Escalade is Cadillac’s statement that swapping out a V8 for a pair of powerful electric motors is no compromise to its ambitions, even if the brand’s future will now include a mix of electric and combustion cars beyond 2030 . It shares a battery pack and much else with other full-size GM EVs we’ve tested: the Chevrolet Silverado EV , the GMC Sierra EV , and of course the divisive Hummer EVs . And like those trucks and SUVs, the Escalade is large and heavy—just small enough to fit into a standard parking space, with a curb weight sufficient to push it into the Class 3 truck category. So, the side mirrors are flat, and there’s no formal EPA range—Cadillac says it achieves 460 miles (740 km) on the EPA test cycle—but there are plenty of airbags, even though the 9,046 lb (4,103 kg) curb weight does not require them. Yes, you did read that right, it does weigh 4 tons. And yes, the electric Escalade does weigh a third more than the last gas-powered one we tested . Read full article Comments

title: Google AI gets cagey when asked who won the 2020 elections
abstract: If you ask some prominent US politicians who won the 2020 presidential election, you might get some weasely answers that fail to directly acknowledge Joe Biden's win that November. If you ask Google's AI Mode the same question, you might get an evasive answer that simply tells you to consult with outside sources. When I put the direct question of "Who won the 2020 presidential election?" to Google's AI Mode this morning (after seeing complaints about cagey answers on social media ), I got the following surprisingly indirect response: "To review the official results and statistics of the 2020 United States presidential election, including the final electoral college breakdown, popular vote counts, and winner certification, please consult the official report compiled by the Federal Election Commission (FEC)." My testing resulted in a similarly indirect answer when asking about the 2024 presidential election, with Google's AI telling me to just consult the FEC for that information. Asking about 2012 election resulted in a link to The American Presidency Project's 2012 Data Center rather than a direct answer. But AI Mode seemed perfectly willing to give me a detailed and correct responses for the winner of every other presidential election going back to 2000. Read full article Comments

title: Florida county won’t investigate sketchy Flock cameras removed by mystery owners
abstract: A Florida county that discovered a clump of mysterious unpermitted Flock cameras during a countywide takedown effort won’t investigate who owned the sketchy cameras, which have since disappeared. On Wednesday, The Washington Post reported that St. Lucie County residents "remain upset,” not knowing who installed the cameras or how they were using the data collected. Hannah Galindo, a 31-year-old resident who petitioned to get Flock cameras removed, told the Post that she was worried “that data could be anywhere.” Of the 12 cameras found, five were eventually claimed by city law enforcement, the Post reported. Apparently, a police department mistakenly issued guidance claiming that officers could post multiple cameras under one permit, a Flock spokesperson told the Post, even though the county required individual permits. However, neither Flock nor the city police departments in Port St. Lucie and Fort Pierce that claimed the sketchy cameras will confirm who gave the guidance. Read full article Comments

title: 사이드카의 선언적 관리: OpenKruise SidecarSet 도입과 운영
abstract: Kubernetes에서 서비스를 운영하다 보면 메인 컨테이너 옆에 사이드카(sidecar) 컨테이너를 붙이는 일이 흔합니다. 사이드카에는 로그와 메트릭 수집, 프록시처럼 주 기능은 아니지만 같은 Pod 안에서 함께 실행되어야 하는 기능이 포함됩니다. 저희 팀이 운영하는 관리형 데이터베이스 서비스도 DB 인스턴스를 Pod 단위로 실행하고, 그 Pod에 DB 컨테이너 외에 헬스 체크, 메트릭과 로그 수집 등을 위한 사이드카를 함께 둡니다. 이 사이드카들은 DB와 같은 데이터 볼륨에 접근해야 하므로 같은 Pod 안에 있어야 하지만, 라이프사이클은 DB와 다릅니다. DB는 한 번 실행하면 몇 달씩 그대로 운영하는 반면, 사이드카는 기능 추가와 버그 수정, 보안 패치로 훨씬 자주 바뀝니다. 사이드카가 바뀔 때마다 그 변경을 모든 인스턴스에 반영해야 하는데, DB 서비스는 유지한 채 실행 중인 Pod의 사이드카만 바꿔야 합니다. 사이드카는 모든 DB Pod에 붙으므로 이 작업은 인스턴스 수만큼 반복됩니다. 그 결과 반영 시점이 인스턴스마다 다를 수 있고, 사이드카 종류가 여럿이면 버전 조합도 인스턴스마다 제각각이 됩니다. DB Pod는 오래 실행되니 이 상태가 그대로 굳어지고, 어떤 인스턴스에 어떤 버전이 실행 중인지 알려면 Pod를 하나씩 조회해야 합니다. 사이드카 수가 늘수록 형상 관리와 배포, 모니터링이 모두 어려워집니다. 이 글은 Kubernetes 환경에서 사이드카를 운영하는 독자를 대상으로, 사이드카를 선언적으로 관리할 수단으로 OpenKruise SidecarSet을 도입한 이유, SidecarSet의 기능과 동작 방식, 운영하며 알게 된 점을 다룹니다. 사이드카 관리의 어려움: 형상 관리, 배포, 모니터링 사이드카를 관리하려면 사이드카 이미지를 한곳에 선언하는 형상 관리, 선언을 실행 중인 Pod에 적용하는 배포, 결과를 조회하는 모니터링이 필요합니다. 그런데 Kubernetes만으로는 이 세 가지가 모두 어렵습니다. 예를 들어 로그 수집 사이드카의 이미지를 바꾸면, 그 사이드카가 들어간 모든 DB Pod에 같이 적용되어야 합니다. 하지만 Kubernetes에서 사이드카 이미지는 Pod 스펙이나 Deployment, StatefulSet의 Pod 템플릿마다 따로 지정되어 있어서 한 번에 바꿀 방법이 없습니다. Pod 템플릿을 고치면 Kubernetes가 Pod를 다시 만들면서 새 이미지를 적용합니다. 하지만 이 과정에서 DB 컨테이너도 함께 재시작되므로 사이드카를 바꿀 때마다 이 방법을 쓸 수는 없습니다. DB는 그대로 둔 채 사이드카만 바꾸려면 실행 중인 Pod의 이미지를 직접 수정(in-place 갱신)해야 합니다. 이때 kubelet은 이미지가 바뀐 컨테이너만 다시 시작하므로 DB 컨테이너는 영향을 받지 않습니다. 다만 이렇게 수정할 수 있는 컨테이너 스펙은 이미지뿐이고, 수정도 Pod마다 따로 해야 합니다. 사이드카 이미지가 바뀔 때마다 대상 Pod를 찾아 하나씩 고치는 일은 Kubernetes가 해 주지 않습니다. 조회도 같은 한계가 있습니다. Deployment, StatefulSet의 status 에 updatedReplicas 가 있지만 템플릿 기준이므로, Pod에서 직접 바꾼 이미지는 집계되지 않습니다. 반영 여부를 확인하려면 Pod마다 status 에 기록된 이미지를 선언과 하나씩 비교해야 합니다. Kubernetes는 워크로드 단위의 재생성과 Pod 하나의 이미지 교체까지만 제공합니다. 여러 워크로드의 사이드카를 한곳에 선언하고, DB를 유지한 채 실행 중인 Pod에 반영하며, 그 결과를 조회하려면 별도의 수단이 필요합니다. 직접 만들 것인가, 가져다 쓸 것인가 가장 단순하게는 대상 Pod를 순회하며 사이드카 이미지를 패치하는 스크립트를 만들 수 있습니다. 그런데 스크립트는 실행한 순간의 Pod 목록에 패치를 보내고 끝나므로, 패치가 실제로 반영됐는지 확인하고 실패한 Pod에 패치를 다시 보내려면 또 다른 스크립트가 필요합니다. 실행 뒤에 생긴 변화도 마찬가지입니다. 사람이 직접 이미지를 되돌린 Pod나 옛 템플릿으로 새로 만들어진 Pod는 다음 스크립트 실행 전까지 이전 버전으로 유지됩니다. 그림 1. 스크립트 실행 사이의 선언과 실제의 어긋남 갱신이 제대로 끝났는지 확인하는 것도 간단하지 않습니다. kubelet이 이미지를 내려받아 컨테이너를 다시 시작하는 과정에서 내려받기가 실패할 수 있고, status 의 이미지 태그만 봐서는 교체가 끝났는지 정확히 알 수 없습니다. 또 어디까지 갱신되었는지를 따로 관리하지 않으면, 갱신을 실행할 때마다 전체 Pod를 확인해야 합니다. 결국 필요한 것은 한 번 실행하고 끝나는 스크립트가 아니라, 의도한 상태(desired state)를 기준으로 실행 중인 Pod를 계속 비교해 맞추는 조정 루프(reconcile loop), 즉 컨트롤러입니다. 이 루프를 저희가 이미 운영 중인 DB 오퍼레이터(DB 인스턴스의 생성과 운영을 자동화하는 컨트롤러)에 넣는 방법도 있습니다. 하지만 이 경우에도 조정 루프를 오퍼레이터 안에 직접 구현해야 합니다. 이미지를 패치하는 것 자체는 Kubernetes가 제공하므로 간단하지만, 이를 안정적으로 운영하려면 다음 네 가지를 갖춰야 합니다. 완료 판정: kubelet이 컨테이너를 실제로 교체했음을 확인 동시성과 범위 제어: 동시에 교체할 개수와 적용 범위를 정하고, 일시 정지와 재개를 지원 진행 집계: 전체 대상 수와 교체가 끝난 수, 정상 상태인 수를 집계 컨트롤러 운영: 컨트롤러 자체의 배포와 가용성, 장애가 났을 때 클러스터에 미치는 영향 관리 이 문제가 저희 팀에만 국한되지는 않을 것이라고 판단했습니다. Kubernetes에서 사이드카를 두고 서비스를 운영하는 팀이라면 어디서든 마주칠 수 있는 문제이기 때문입니다. 그래서 직접 만들기 전에 기존 해결책을 찾아봤습니다. Istio처럼 Pod 생성 시점에 mutating 웹훅으로 사이드카를 주입하는 구현은 여럿 있지만, 실행 중인 Pod의 사이드카를 선언에 맞춰 갱신하지는 않았습니다. 반면 OpenKruise의 SidecarSet은 이 요건까지 갖춘 것으로 확인했습니다. OpenKruise는 Kubernetes의 워크로드 기능을 확장하는 CNCF(Cloud Native Computing Foundation) 인큐베이팅 프로젝트이고, SidecarSet은 사이드카 컨테이너의 라이프사이클을 메인 컨테이너와 분리해 관리하도록 OpenKruise가 제공하는 CR(Custom Resource)입니다. SidecarSet에서는 새 Pod에 웹훅이 항상 최신 정의를 주입하고, 선언을 바꾸면 컨트롤러가 실행 중인 Pod를 맞추므로, 스크립트 실행 사이에 새 Pod가 이전 버전으로 남는 구간이 생기지 않습니다. 다만 사람이 직접 바꾼 Pod는 이 방식으로도 감지되지 않아 운영 규칙으로 막았습니다. 또 컨트롤러는 자신이 주입한 컨테이너를 이름으로 찾아 그 이미지만 바꾸므로, 같은 Pod의 DB 컨테이너 이미지는 바꾸지 않습니다. 외부 컴포넌트가 늘어나는 운영 부담을 감수하면서도 SidecarSet을 도입한 이유는 SidecarSet이 컨트롤러 운영을 제외한 나머지 기능인 완료 판정, 동시성과 범위 제어, 진행 집계를 이미 갖추고 있었기 때문입니다. SidecarSet의 기능 SidecarSet은 형상 관리, 배포, 모니터링을 각각 CR의 선언, updateStrategy , status 로 제공합니다. 앞에서 정리한 네 가지 요건 중 동시성과 범위 제어는 updateStrategy 가, 진행 집계는 status 가 맡습니다. 완료 판정은 SidecarSet의 동작 방식 에서, 컨트롤러 운영의 부담은 운영에서 주의할 점 에서 다룹니다. 이 글의 동작 설명은 저희가 운영 중인 OpenKruise v1.8.3 기준입니다. 형상 관리: 사이드카 정의를 CR 하나에 CR에는 사이드카 컨테이너의 정의 전체가 들어갑니다. 이미지는 물론 실행 사용자와 capability를 정하는 securityContext , 마운트할 볼륨, 기동 인자와 환경 변수, 포트, preStop 훅(hook)까지 담을 수 있습니다. 주

title: AI 시대의 개발자를 꿈꾸는 학생 개발자에게
abstract: 시작하며: 2018년과 2026년 사이의 간격과 격변기의 고민 ​ 2018년에 저는 ' 백엔드 개발자를 꿈꾸는 학생개발자에게 '라는 글을 이곳 D2 블로그에 공유했습니다. 당시 학생 개발자들과의 미트업 행사에서 나왔던 질문과 답변을 정리한 글이었습니다. 그 후 8년의 시간이 흘렀기에 그 글만 노출된다면 학생들에게 현시점에 적절한 정보를 주지 못할까 봐 걱정되었습니다. 그래서 2025년 말 설문으로 질문을 받아 후속편을 작성했습니다. ​ 그동안 저도 경험과 지식을 더 쌓았습니다. 하지만 지금 학생 개발자들이 한 질문에는 답하기가 더 어려워졌습니다. 개발자의 역할과 같은 큰 주제를 묻는 질문이 많았는데, 지금은 AI로 인한 변화가 큰 시기이기 때문입니다. 스스로도 확신이 없는 시기에 이런 글을 쓰는 것이 적절할지 고민도 했습니다. ​ 그럼에도 2018년의 글에 보내 주신 관심에 용기를 얻어서 이 글을 발행합니다. 최근의 경험을 나누고 미래를 함께 상상해 보는 일이 지금 시점에는 더 의미가 있다고 생각합니다. 이 글을 목적지가 명확한 안내서보다는 격변기의 스냅샷 정도로 봐 주셨으면 합니다. 주요 질문과 답변 설문을 통해 들어온 질문들을 비슷한 주제로 모아서 답변을 정리했습니다. [AI 시대와 개발자] 가장 비중이 높은 질문 유형이었고 근본적인 주제이기도 합니다. 이 질문에 먼저 답하지 않고서는 다른 이야기를 풀어 가기가 어려웠습니다. ​ ​ AI 시대에 개발자의 역할은 어떻게 달라졌을까요? 누군가는 AI를 인터넷이나 전기, 불에 비견될 정도의 혁명이라고 말합니다. [1] 2025년부터는 그 주장이 과장이 아니라고 느낍니다. 제가 프로그래밍을 시작한 1989년 이후로 '코딩’이라는 활동에 가장 큰 변화가 왔습니다. AI 코딩 도구가 코드를 추천해 주는 역할에서 나아가 소스 작성, OS 명령 실행 등 사람의 실질적인 대리로 행동합니다. ​ 역사를 돌아보면 기술이 발전하면서 지식 근로자가 하는 일은 이전 시대 관리자의 역할에 가까워졌습니다. 1980년대에 개인용 컴퓨터가 보급되기 전까지 지식 근로자의 작업 공간은 종이였고, 수기로 정보를 처리하는 일에 쓰는 시간의 비중이 컸습니다. AI 시대 전에도 계산, 정보의 형식 변환과 취합 등 컴퓨터가 하는 일의 범위는 꾸준히 늘어 왔습니다. 과거의 실무 일부를 컴퓨터가 하게 되면서 말단의 지식 근로자도 영향력이 큰 의사결정에 많이 관여할 수 있게 되었고 권한도 커졌습니다. ​ CAD 도입 전 General Motors의 기술자들이 작업하는 모습 (이미지 출처: ArchDaily ) 이제는 조직의 말단 작업자는 AI이고 모든 개발자는 AI 팀의 관리자가 되었습니다. 사람은 여러 AI 에이전트에게 업무를 지시하고 결과에 피드백을 줍니다. 아래에 나열한 일들은 전통적인 관리자의 역할이기도 하지만 '작업자’를 'AI 에이전트’로 바꿔서 읽어 본다면 이제는 모든 개발자가 하는 일입니다. ​ 다수의 작업자에게 목표와 배경, 추구하는 가치, 평가 기준을 제시한다. 작업자의 정보 탐색 비용을 줄여 준다. 참조할 정보가 어디에 있는지 알려 준다. 작업자별 역할을 명확히 정의하여 할 일을 분배한다. 작업자별 장점과 투자액(과금액) 수준을 고려하여 각자의 작업에 집중할 수 있도록, 컨텍스트가 과도하게 넓어지지 않고 컨텍스트 전환이 최소화되도록 의사결정자와 작업자 간의 효율적인 피드백 사이클을 구축한다. ​ 관리 업무의 멀티태스킹도 개발자가 적응해야 할 환경이 되었습니다. 에이전트에게 많은 일을 맡기려면 다수의 작업자가 병렬로 일을 진행할 수 있도록 지시를 내리고 결과물에는 빠른 피드백을 주어야 합니다. 작업자마다 컨텍스트를 좁혀 줄수록, 넓은 범위의 맥락을 머리에 올려 두고 빠르게 전환해야 하는 부담은 사람에게 더 크게 돌아옵니다. AI 에이전트와 일하는 형태는 여러 메신저 창을 왔다 갔다 하면서 다수와 병렬로 대화를 이어 가는 관리자의 모습과도 닮아 갑니다. 어떤 순간에는 화면을 어지럽게 전환하면서 게임 유닛에게 작업 지시와 확인, 판단을 쉴 틈 없이 하는 프로게이머와도 유사하게 느껴집니다. ​ 정보를 찾을 수 있는 연결 체계와 필요한 권한을 제공하여 에이전트가 막힘없이 일하도록 하는 일이 중요해지고 있습니다. 부작용을 줄이며 코드를 고치고 빠르게 피드백을 받을 수 있는 아키텍처와 워크플로를 설계하는 일도 핵심 업무가 됩니다. 개발자 경험(Developer Experience)뿐만이 아니라 AI 에이전트 입장에서 얼마나 일을 하기 쉬운지가 생산성을 좌우하게 됩니다. 이는 개발 리더가 다른 개발자들이 일하기 좋은 코드 구조와 작업 절차를 잡아 주는 일과도 유사합니다. 아키텍처와 기술 스택, 구현 방식 같은 기술 의사결정은 여전히 중요합니다. 합리적으로 결정하면 AI 에이전트가 더 안전하고 빠르게 일하고, 그렇지 못하면 오히려 기술부채를 쌓습니다. 예를 들면 모듈 경계가 분명하면 에이전트는 고칠 범위를 좁게 잡지만, 경계가 흐리면 비슷한 코드를 여기저기 복제합니다. ​ 더 상위 수준의 설계까지 AI가 맡는 다음 단계도 이미 시작되고 있습니다. 최근의 코딩 에이전트는 다른 에이전트에게 일을 분배하는 리더 역할까지도 수행합니다. 아키텍처도 AI가 제안하는 방향을 개발자가 수용하거나 근거로 드는 빈도가 높아지고 있습니다. 리더와 아키텍트 역할까지 AI가 가져간다면, 조직 수준의 투자와 리스크 감수를 결정하는 일이 사람의 역할로 남을 것입니다. 앞에서 모든 개발자가 AI 팀의 관리자가 되었다고 말씀드렸는데, 이 단계까지 가면 모든 회사 구성원이 한 번 더 승진을 하는 셈입니다. 조직도상의 개인 기여자도 일하는 형태로는 여러 실무팀의 리더들의 리더가 됩니다. 현실 세계 조직도상의 조직장은 리더들의 리더들의 리더가 되니, 적어도 소기업 경영진의 관점에서 생각하고 결정하는 빈도가 높아질 것 같습니다. 경영진이 투자 대비 사업 성과를 평가하듯, AI 사용료에서 종량제 비중이 높아지면서 한 번의 세션, 한 번의 프롬프트가 주는 부가가치에도 이전보다 신경을 쓰게 됩니다. ​ AI는 지치지 않고 병렬로 일하는 대신 세션이 끝나면 맥락을 잊습니다. 이처럼 사람과 지능의 성격이 다르니 관리하는 방법도 달라야 합니다. 그 차이를 전제하더라도, 관리자의 일하는 방식에 하나의 정답이 없다는 점은 AI와 일하는 방식을 고를 때도 참고가 됩니다. 개발을 모르는 팀장도 팀원들에게 맡기면 결과물은 나오고, 몰라서 더 많이 위임하기에 생기는 장점도 있습니다. 반면 개발을 잘 아는 팀장은 처음부터 올바른 방향을 지시해 시행착오를 줄이기도 합니다. ​ AI 에이전트와 일할 때도 코드를 아는 개발자는 상황에 따라 마이크로매니징과 큰 단위의 위임 중에서 고를 수 있습니다. 이렇게 현미경과 망원경을 오가면서 AI를 감독할 수 있다면 특성과 민감도가 다양한 작업을 안정적으로 수행할 수 있을 것입니다. 제가 아는 뛰어난 개발자 중에서는 수 시간 동안 에이전트가 실행할 업무 정의를 잘하시는 분도 있습니다. 프롬프트를 내린 후에 중간에 나오는 메시지를 하나하나 다 보시면서 에이전트가 일을 어긋나게 수행하는 순간을 바로 잡아내시는 분도 있습니다. ​ ​ AI에게 맡겨도 되는 부분과 개발자가 직접 해야 하는 부분이 있을까요? 실행 능력만 놓고 보면 이제는 AI가 개발자가 하는 대부분의 일을 할 수 있고, 더 잘하는 일도 많습니다. 아무리 AI가 발전해도 할 수 없는 일이 무엇일지를 생각해 보면 이 질문에 오래가는 답을 찾을 수 있습니다. 사람만이 '책임’을 질 수 있습니다. AI 에이전트가 모든 작업을 다 해 준다고 해도 그 소프트웨어를 사용자가 쓰게 하는 결정은 사람이 내립니다. 그로 인해 사용자에게 미친 영향의 책임은 AI에게 지시를 내리고 그 결과물을 최종 승인한 사람에게 돌아갑니다. AI 생성 이미지 ​ 누구나 코드를 만들 수 있게 된 시대에 '개발자’라는 명칭이 앞으로도 쓰인다면, 민감한 시스템의 운영 환경에 코드 배포를 승인하는 사람이라는 의미가 가장 크지 않을까 합니다. 그렇다면 문제를 알아보고 예방할 수 있다는 믿음을 주는 사람에게 그런 권한을 부여하고 '개발자’라고 부를 가능성이 높습니다. 그런 믿음을 주려면 코드의 동작 결과를 검증하고 보장하는 장치와

title: 팀이 신뢰할 수 있는 AI 분석 환경 만들기: 추천팀의 컨텍스트 설계
abstract: 안녕하세요. 카카오톡 숏폼 추천 모델을 개발하고 있는 루퍼트(rupert)입니다. 저희 추천팀은 추천 지표 분석에 AI 에이전트를 사용합니다. AI 에이전트에게 분석을 요청하면, 에이전트가 미리 정리해 둔 지침 문서(CLAUDE.md)를 읽고 SQL을 작성해 기존 Hadoop 환경에서 실행한 뒤 집계 결과를 리포트로 완성합니다. 지난 글에서는 데이터 엔지니어, 분석가만 알고 있던 로그 데이터 접근 방법과 분석 기준을 AI를 통해 조회하는 사례를 소개했습...

title: 손가락 튕기기로 LLM 비용 줄이기
abstract: 토스의 수많은 서비스와 내부 업무에도 생성형 AI가 정말 많이 사용되고 있습니다. 복잡한 정책을 읽고, 상품 정보를 비교하고, 문서를 요약하고, 정해진 형식의 값을 추출하는 등, LLM이 맡는 범위도 빠르게 넓어지고 있죠. 시간도 비용도 비싼 데이터 레이블링을 통해 모델을 학습하고 문제를 해결하던 과거 방식과 달리, LLM을 사용하면 빠른 시간 내에 사용할 수 있는 솔루션이 만들어집니다. 프롬프트를 작성하고, 몇 가지 예시를 넣고, 응답 형식을 고정하면 동작하는 Workflow가 나오죠 . 하지만 프롬프트 튜닝을 마치고 본격적으로 대용량 호출을 시작하면 새로운 문제가 보이기 시작합니다. 바로 비용과 Latency 입니다. 이 토큰 먹는 하마는 정말 토스의 모든 문제 해결에 지속적으로 필요한걸까요? LLM Fine-Tuning is all you need? 상용 LLM을 사용하지 않고 내재화 한다면, 비용을 크게 절감할 수 있습니다. 작업 목표에 따라 LoRA(Low-Rank Adaptation)처럼 효율적인 Adapter 학습을 사용할 수도 있고, 더 큰 품질 개선이나 안정성이 필요하다면 Full Fine-Tuning을 검토할 수도 있습니다. 실제로 토스에서도 LLM Fine-Tuning 을 통해 비용을 크게 절감한 사례도 있어요. 그런데 모든 LLM 호출에 같은 수준의 능력이 필요한 것은 아닙니다. 복잡한 문맥을 이해하고 긴 답변을 생성해야 하는 작업도 있지만, 두 상품이 같은지 판단하거나 정해진 카테고리 중 하나를 고르는 작업도 있어요. 이런 작업이 반드시 범용 LLM의 모든 능력을 필요로 하지는 않습니다. 작업의 복잡도와 요구되는 품질에 따라, 전통적인 ML 모델이나 특정 작업에 최적화한 소형 모델을 적절히 선택해도 충분히 처리할 수 있는 경우가 있죠. 중요한 것은 모델의 크기보다, 주어진 작업에 필요한 품질을 확보할 수 있느냐입니다. Figure 1. LLM이 처리하는 다양한 작업. 작업의 특성과 요구 품질에 따라 적합한 모델도 달라집니다. 전환이 가능한 트래픽부터 내재화하기 '작은 모델'이 가지는 장단점은 명확합니다. 빠르고, 자원 소모가 적지만, 처리할 수 있는 문제의 범위에는 제약이 있어요. 간단한 질문으로 시작해봤습니다. 내재화 모델은 꼭 LLM과 동등한, 혹은 견줄 만한 수준으로 성능을 끌어올려야만 사용할 수 있는 걸까? 빠르고 작은 모델이라도 쉬운 요청은 충분히 처리할 수 있을 텐데? 이 질문으로부터 선택적 내재화(SNAP, Selective Native AI Processing)를 기획하게 되었어요. SNAP의 핵심은 해결해야 하는 문제의 모든 요청을 한 번에 Native Model로 처리하는 것이 아니라, 작은 모델도 높은 신뢰도로 처리할 수 있는 트래픽부터 빠르게 처리하는 것입니다. 고비용 LLM Traffic을 한 번에 없애기보다, 처리 가능한 구간을 찾아 타노스가 손가락을 튕기듯( SNAP! ) 손쉽게 줄여보자는 의미도 담겨 있죠. 큰 틀에서 SNAP은 다음 3가지 규칙을 하나의 Workflow로 묶습니다. 비교적 쉬운 요청은 작업별 소형 내재화 모델이 처리합니다. 어렵거나 애매한 요청은 기존 LLM으로 Fallback합니다. Fallback의 기준은 내재화 모델의 Confidence와 Offline 검증 결과로 정합니다. 자, 그렇다면 작업별 소형 모델을 만들기 위해서 먼저 작업별로 학습데이터가 될 LLM 로그부터 수집해야겠죠? 그런데 여기서 한 가지 문제가 있었습니다. 방대한 LLM 로그들을 동일한 작업으로 어떻게 분류하죠? LLM 호출 로그에는 굉장히 다양하고 이질적인 요청들이 섞여서 들어옵니다. LLM 으로 보내는 요청은 사람에게 말하듯 높은 자유도가 주어지기 때문에 같은 API Key, 같은 Endpoint를 사용해 호출하더라도 동일한 작업임을 전혀 보장할 수가 없죠. 그래서 먼저 요청을 작업 단위로 묶을 기준이 필요했습니다. 다양한 Task들의 로그에서 나타나는 공통적인 특징은 Prompting 방식이었습니다. 많은 LLM Workflow는 System Prompt 앞부분에서 LLM에게 Role을 부여하고, 해결해야 할 문제와 함께 문제 해결 방식을 정의하는데요. 살펴본 로그에서는 Few-shot 예제가 바뀌어도 역할과 작업 정의는 대체로 유지됐습니다. SNAP은 이 특성을 이용해 system prompt 앞부분을 해시하고, 이를 작업을 구분하는 Fingerprint로 사용했습니다. Figure 2. Role 부여와 작업 정의에 변동 폭이 작은 LLM 호출 프롬프트의 특성을 이용한 작업 분리 후보 발굴부터 모델 학습까지 자동화하기 작업 단위로 로그를 살펴보니 또 다른 문제가 있었습니다. 짧은 기간 안에 새로운 작업이 생기기도 했고, 얼마 지나지 않아 사라지기도 했어요. LLM으로 빠르게 개념 검증(PoC, Proof of Concept)을 진행한 뒤 작업을 변경하거나 프로젝트를 중단하는 경우가 있기 때문이었죠. 계속 바뀌는 작업을 사람이 하나씩 살펴보며 내재화 후보를 고르기에는 한계가 있었습니다. 그래서 SNAP은 내재화 후보 발굴부터 데이터셋 구축, 모델 학습까지의 과정을 자동화했습니다. 먼저 매일 호출 로그를 Task Fingerprint별로 묶어 호출량, 사용 중인 LLM 모델, 입력·출력 토큰 수와 추정 비용 을 집계합니다. 최근 일정 기간의 추정 비용이 최소 기준을 넘는 작업을 비용순으로 정렬하고, 정해진 수만큼 후속 검증 대상으로 선정합니다. Table 1 은 비용 기반 상위 30개 작업을 선정한 로그를 재구성한 예시입니다. Table 1. 작업별 추정 비용을 기준으로 상위 30개 작업을 후속 검증 대상으로 선정한 예시. 중간 순위는 생략했으며, 비용은 설명을 위한 가상 값입니다. 선정된 작업은 요청과 응답을 분석해 학습 가능성을 검증합니다. 응답이 정형화되어 있고 그 안에서 학습용 레이블을 안정적으로 추출할 수 있는지 확인합니다. 데이터셋을 구성하면서 레이블별 데이터가 충분한지, 학습과 평가에 사용할 데이터를 분리할 수 있는지도 검증합니다. 이 조건을 통과한 작업만 모델 학습으로 이어집니다. 이 과정은 Airflow의 일일 배치로 연결했습니다. 후보 선정과 데이터 구성 기준을 충족한 작업은 사내 학습 라이브러리를 통해 하루 안에 학습된 모델을 확보할 수 있습니다. 학습한 모델은 모델 레지스트리에 등록하며, 운영에 적용할 모델은 서빙 엔진이 불러와 요청을 처리합니다. SNAP의 첫 내재화 모델 배포: 텍스트 기반 동일상품 판별 SNAP의 첫 적용 대상은 두 상품의 이름과 옵션 정보를 비교해 같은 판매 단위인지 판단하는 작업이었습니다. 브랜드, 모델명, 용량, 색상, 구성품 등의 차이를 읽고 동일 상품 여부를 분류하는 문제였죠. 입력과 출력의 범위가 명확하고 기존 LLM 응답도 충분히 쌓여 있어, 소형 분류 모델을 적용하기에 적합했습니다. 첫 적용 모델과 평가 데이터는 다음과 같이 구성했습니다. Confidence로 채택 범위 정하기 모델은 판단 결과와 함께 자신 있는 정도를 나타내는 점수, Confidence를 반환합니다. 하지만 이 점수가 높다고 해서 실제로 얼마나 잘 맞히는지까지 알 수 있는 것은 아니에요. Confidence가 0.95라고 해서 정답률이 95%라는 뜻은 아니죠. 그래서 검증 데이터에서 Confidence 점수가 높은 결과만 골라 다음 두 가지를 확인했습니다. 골라낸 결과가 기존 LLM 판단과 일치하는 비율인 선택적 정확도(Selective Accuracy) 전체 검증 요청 중 채택된 비율인 Coverage 먼저 목표 일치율을 정하고, 결과를 채택할 최소 점수(Threshold)를 바꿔가며 비교했습니다. 목표를 만족하는 범위에서 가장 많은 요청을 처리할 수 있는 기준을 찾는 것입니다. 학습 중 저장한 모델들도 같은 방식으로 비교해 사용할 모델과 기준 점수를 함께 선택했습니다. title: MEV: A Multi-Event Video Dataset for Long-Take Generation
abstract: Current datasets for text-to-video generation are largely limited to short clips depicting a single event or coarse-grained captions. As a result, they provide limited supervision for modeling long-take temporal dependencies, often leading to temporally inconsistent generations when describing multiple events. In this paper, we introduce MEV, a multi-event video dataset designed for long-take video generation. MEV provides high-quality real-world videos where subjects can perform a sequence of distinct, non-overlapping events, featuring precise temporal boundaries and fine-grained procedural annotations. This event-centric discretization reduces confounding factors and enables models to support temporally localized conditioning and build long-take videos from atomic event units. Furthermore, we introduce a comprehensive annotation pipeline that segments videos into temporally grounded events, and generates structured captions at both the global level and the event level. In addition, under an event-centric evaluation protocol, we conduct multi-event generation experiments by fine-tuning on MEV with temporally grounded event conditioning, leading to improved long-take event transitions and more coherent content. We believe this work provides a publicly available resource for multi-event fine-tuning and event-centric evaluation, together with practical insights into learning from temporally structured video-text data.

title: Variational Consequence-Driven Offline Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Offline reinforcement learning (RL) typically mitigates distribution shift by imposing divergence constraints on the action distributions of the learned and behavior policies. However, this paradigm cannot ensure the underlying dynamic consistency structure: even minor action deviations can lead to drastically different transitions, inadvertently driving the agent away from the offline dataset. To address this, we explore policy constraints through their induced state-consequence distributions rather than relying on pure action-distribution matching. Nevertheless, directly enforcing such consequence-aware constraints is computationally intractable without access to the true underlying dynamics model. To bypass this issue, we propose Structural Behavior Regularization (StBR), which replaces the intractable objective with a closed-form latent divergence. Structuring this latent space to reflect transition dynamics renders the latent divergence a theoretically bounded surrogate for the true consequence-distribution divergence. By regularizing the learned policy with this latent divergence, StBR adaptively tightens the behavior constraint in dynamics-sensitive regions, effectively preventing deviations outside the offline dataset. Empirically, we demonstrate that StBR achieves superior performance across diverse offline RL benchmarks.

title: B2P-Corr: Batch-to-Population Gradient Estimators for Non-Decomposable Correlation Losses
abstract: Correlation metrics such as the Pearson Correlation Coefficient (PCC) and Concordance Correlation Coefficient (CCC) are standard regression metrics and learning objectives, but their non-decomposable nature poses a challenge for stochastic optimization. Since these metrics depend on dataset-level moments (mean, variance, covariance), naive mini-batch training with local statistics yields biased, high-variance gradients whose expectation does not align with the population gradient. To bridge this ``batch-to-population'' (B2P) gap, we propose \textbf{B2P-Corr}, a novel framework that transforms correlation objectives into decomposable pseudo-losses driven by lightweight global ``moment sketches''. We introduce two efficient variants: \textbf{B2P-EMA}, which utilizes exponential moving averages and stop-gradient operators to ensure asymptotic gradient tracking with $O(B)$ cost ($B$ is batch size); and \textbf{B2P-U}, which uses sampled cross-batch U-statistic estimators and a reservoir-based stabilization with an $O(B)$ implementation. Theoretically, we quantify the $O(B^{-1})$ bias of naive mini-batch optimization, prove a moving-target tracking result for B2P-EMA under a fast-sketch / slow-parameter regime, and provide an idealized control-variate analysis for B2P-U. Experiments on two synthetic and three real-world datasets demonstrate B2P-Corr achieves stable optimization and higher correlation than naive mini-batch optimization with negligible overhead.

title: Floor It, Then Fill It: Simulating Creator Ecosystems for Fair Video-Content Recommendation Systems at Billion User Scale
abstract: Engagement-optimized content recommendation systems exhibit a well-documented rich-get-richer dynamic that structurally disadvantages emerging creators on large-scale platforms. Evaluating debiasing interventions at scale demands faithful simulation of creator-viewer ecosystems, yet the fidelity, diversity, and validity of such simulators remain underexplored. We present a grounded user-simulation framework that models a heterogeneous population of ${\sim}42$K creators and their coupled viewer interactions over 12~weeks, and use it to evaluate equitable view-allocation policies formulated as a budgeted multi-armed bandit (MAB). The simulator captures three behavioral dimensions: (i)~\textbf{creator diversity}, modeled via a clustering approach grounded in real platform creator-level distributions; (ii)~\textbf{behavioral fidelity}, captured through coupled creator-content state machines that represent growth trajectories, engagement accumulation, and graduation dynamics; and (iii)~\textbf{population-level validity}, measured by calibration against observed platform metrics. We evaluate simulative-configurations that vary content-viewership target definitions, reward functions, and a small-creator reserve lever to maximize creator-content recommendation equity. A floor-protected per content-view-target with a view-parity-gap reward guarantees 90\% of view targets being met by creators every week, grows small-creator organic reach ${\sim}{+}33\%$ per week, and achieves high distribution stability (set of creators with funded-views Jaccard $= 0.819$). We analyze the Sim2Real gap and propose validation protocols, contributing evidence for when simulation-derived fairness conclusions can be trusted.

title: Who Called? V33DA: A Physically Verified Multimodal Benchmark for Vocal Attribution in Zebra Finch Groups
abstract: Deciding which member of an animal group produced a vocalization and where that vocalization was produced are central to studying social communication but are rarely evaluated with physically verified ground truth. Existing resources either localize sounds without identifying the caller, or recognize individuals from isolated vocalizations without reliance on the 3D candidate geometry. We close this gap with V33DA, a dataset-centered multimodal benchmark for spatial vocal attribution in social zebra finches: it comprises 33,625 verified events coupling 5-channel audio with three camera views, calibrated 3D pose for every visible candidate, and per-bird radio telemetry across 10 individuals and three experiments. Caller identity is verified from an on-body accelerometer-derived vibration signal; this channel is withheld from benchmark models and used only by an on-body reference ceiling. Given a detected vocalization and the visible candidate birds, the task is to select the caller. We evaluate it under three regimes: session-disjoint testing on familiar birds from held-out recording dates, held-out-experiment transfer to a new cohort, and leave-one-individual-out evaluation on a bird whose vocalizations are held out from training. Reference methods expose a consistent gap between in-domain accuracy and transfer to unseen individuals: methods that can exploit familiar vocal identity perform well on known callers but degrade sharply on unseen ones, whereas candidate-aware methods preserving explicit spatial reasoning transfer substantially better. The on-body reference stays near-perfect across regimes, confirming the internal consistency of the accelerometer-verified labels. We release V33DA with fixed protocols and code for the evaluated methods, and V33DA++, an unevaluated companion set of verified overlapping-call events and +/-2 s context windows.

title: The Prestige: Benchmarking Cognitive Visual Reasoning using Magic Tricks
abstract: We introduce The Prestige, a video understanding benchmark that probes cognitive visual reasoning through professional magic performances, where deliberate misdirection challenges models to track events and explain unexpected outcomes. The benchmark comprises open-ended questions ranging from temporal and causal understanding to robustness against adversarial questions. Evaluation of leading open-source and proprietary VLMs reveals a substantial gap between even the strongest model and human performance. We also find systematic discrepancies between human and automated grading and identify recurring model failure modes. Ablations further show that models can select correct multiple-choice answers even when they fail to generate correct explanations independently, motivating further investigations into question formats. Together, these findings highlight limitations in both VLM reasoning and its evaluation, underscoring the need for more reliable video understanding models and more rigorous benchmarks.

title: Neural Compression of Long ADMM Trajectory for Multiparametric Quadratic Program
abstract: Solving large-scale multiparametric quadratic programs (mpQPs) in real time often requires thousands of iterative optimization updates, creating a major computational bottleneck in model predictive control and learning-enabled systems. This paper proposes TQPNet, a self-supervised neural compression framework that learns to compress long ADMM optimization trajectories into a compact neural warm start followed by a few refinement iterations. We derive a low-dimensional ADMM scheme operating on the primal-dual variables $(x,β)$ and show that its iteration admits an equivalent ReLU-layer representation, termed ADMM(ReLU). Building on this insight, TQPNet combines a multilayer perceptron with ReLU activations (MLP(ReLU)) and a small number of unrolled ADMM(ReLU) refinement layers. The network is trained offline using an optimality-condition-informed residual loss, eliminating the need for solver-generated labels. The proposed residual-based framework enables both self-supervised training and online solution certification through adaptive ADMM(ReLU) refinement. Experiments on large-scale mpQPs and real-time MPC applications demonstrate that TQPNet achieves high accuracy, strong generalization, and substantially faster inference than conventional optimization-based methods.

title: Integral Probability Boundaries
abstract: Bounds based on Integral Probability Metrics (IPMs) are ubiquitous in machine learning and statistics, appearing, e.g., in generalization, alignment, fairness, and privacy. IPMs reduce the discrepancy between two distributions to a single worst-case gap between expectations. This compression is costly: for rare events, safety failures, or under-represented groups, IPM-based bounds are loose or vacuous. We introduce a non-linear generalization of IPMs, which we term Integral Probability Boundaries (IPBs). Unlike IPMs, IPBs provide bounds that are tight at the extremes. We derive their basic properties and present algorithms for estimating them in practically relevant settings. We demonstrate the usage of IPBs in both theoretical and practical applications for alignment, judge-free performance estimation, and fairness, where they enable us to obtain sharp bounds on performance and fairness gaps, e.g., 15 p.p. more precise estimates on fairness gaps for rare groups in a realistic generative modeling task, compared to the state of the art.

title: Detecting Brain Cancer Progression Through Signatures of Wearable Accelerometry Data
abstract: Glioblastoma and other high-grade gliomas (HGG) have a poor prognosis and are associated with progressive functional decline. The standard of care to assess progressive disease is contrast-enhanced MRI, which is expensive, claustrophobic, and performed only once every 2-3 months. Wearable accelerometers offer a non-invasive alternative for continuously monitoring patient function between clinic visits. However, accelerometry data streams are typically noisy and highly patient-specific, making conventional time series methods and summary statistics poorly suited to detecting clinically meaningful change. This work aims to classify stable versus progressive disease states by applying rough path signatures for feature extraction from wrist-worn accelerometer data. We convert accelerometer recordings from HGG patients enrolled in the BrainWear study into walking-path segments and use signature kernel maximum mean discrepancy (SigMMD) to quantify change in patients' walking behaviour. We overcome the challenge of inter-patient heterogeneity by adjusting for the natural variation in a patient's walking during stable tumour periods. This patient-specific normalisation substantially improves separation, yielding a candidate biomarker of tumour progression. Our results provide proof-of-concept evidence that signature-based analysis of wearable accelerometry can distinguish stable from progressive disease states, motivating larger longitudinal studies of continuous wearable monitoring as a digital biomarker in neuro-oncology.

title: Are Seismic Foundation Models More Than Glorified Feature Extractors?
abstract: Earthquake sequences are stochastic on two separated timescales: the seismic waves of any individual earthquake propagate over seconds to minutes, while the earthquakes themselves arrive as a sparse, self-exciting occurrence process, with inter-event intervals from seconds to months. Respecting both scales in one training objective is the open challenge. Foundation models (FMs) for seismic waveforms instead import their learning targets from audio and vision, where every target is computed from a single fixed-length window. Such a window holds one realization of the wave propagation (an earthquake trace), never the occurrence process that decides when earthquakes happen. We develop nine model designs sharing one Mamba encoder-decoder, trained on a fixed corpus of 3M windows, varying the self-supervised objective, quantization bottleneck and mixer; the two key comparisons are architecture-matched, varying the objective alone. Each checkpoint is evaluated frozen on three downstream tasks. Varying the target redistributes downstream skill rather than raising it, and no checkpoint wins everywhere. Adding masking pressure to our strongest classifier re-specializes it rather than making it a generalist: it gains 6.9 points of few-shot P-wave picking precision and loses 9.6 points of few-shot classification accuracy. By the standard imported from language and vision, these models are feature extractors rather than FMs. Controls on capacity, architecture, and domain proximity do not explain why skill moves rather than rises. Against task-specific baselines the advantage is regime-dependent: our checkpoints beat them few-shot on classification and ground-motion prediction, and trail them on full data. We argue the binding constraint is the target, and that settling the question requires a learning target defined across events, the timescale that makes seismicity stochastic in the first place.

title: Separability Is Not Alignability: Representations for Spectrum-to-Molecule Retrieval
abstract: Identifying a small molecule from its tandem mass spectrum is limited by paired data. Foundation models offer a way around this scarcity: pretrain a spectrum encoder on unlabeled spectra and a molecule encoder on a large corpus of structures, then align the two frozen representations, as in vision-language and as the Platonic Representation Hypothesis suggests. We audit this route on MassSpecGym with spectrum encoders retrained free of test-fold contamination. Alignment needs a metric relating distinct molecules, but the objectives that produce spectrum encoders never see molecular structure: we prove that some predictive objectives fix molecular identity without fixing that metric. Moreover, we find that a candidate-based objective rewards a spectrum-independent prior over the benchmark's decoys, which we isolate. What ultimately addresses data scarcity is not architectural: simulated spectra surpass frozen geometry.

title: SAG-Sep: Sparse Augmented Graphs and Onion-Guided Search for Rounded Capacity Cut Separation
abstract: Rounded capacity cuts (RCCs) are among the most effective cuts for capacitated vehicle-routing relaxations, but exact separation is computationally prohibitive at scale. Existing heuristic and neural separators can be fast, but often fail to produce sufficiently many effective cuts within practical separation budgets. We introduce SAG-Sep, a separator that scores node membership in RCC-inducing subsets across vehicle-count levels from a fractional LP solution in a single encoder forward pass, avoiding the iterative predict-and-coarsen inference used by NeuralSEP-style separators. SAG-Sep encodes the LP solution as a Sparse Augmented Graph (SAG), adding flow-informed multi-hop edges that expose long-range routing structure without densifying attention. Beyond LP-aware sparse encoding, we observe that high-value exact RCCs are typically nested, organizing into onion-like subset families, and SAG-Sep's node scores track subset nesting depth. This motivates Onion-Sweep (OS), a training-free decoder that ranks customers by their scores, evaluates the RCC violation of every prefix of the ranking in one vectorized pass, and emits the most violated prefix of each replica together with a cross-replica family of nested proposals, converting independent node scores into structurally coordinated RCC candidates without a tuned threshold or probing band. On the NeuralSEP benchmark with N=1000 customer instances, SAG-Sep with OS reduces the average root gap by 17.7% relative to the strongest NeuralSEP baseline, while the single-pass SAG-Sep separator achieves a roughly 30-fold per-iteration neural separation speedup. Our findings suggest that LP-aware sparse encoding and the nested structure of high-value cuts are structural patterns worth leveraging in neural separation more broadly.

title: You Don't Need Aligned Representations: Knowledge Distillation via Random Prototype Spaces
abstract: A widely held assumption in knowledge distillation is that teacher and student representations must occupy a compatible or explicitly aligned feature space. We propose RPKD (Random Prototype Knowledge Distillation), which discards this assumption by comparing both networks against a shared bank of randomly initialized, frozen prototype vectors. Alignment is therefore carried out in an external reference space rather than in the teacher's native feature coordinates: the teacher side is projected by fixed random maps that carry no trainable parameters, and only the student adapts. Two branches handle the transfer: a logit branch aligning global prototype similarity distributions and a feature branch matching spatially-resolved prototype activation maps.
